listing.name: Star Wars: X-Wing (OpenXW)
listing.summary: A native engine for Star Wars: X-Wing using your own original game data.

presentation.manual_preparation: On Play, keep the normal in-process setup picker. Select your own complete 1994 Collector’s CD-ROM and/or 1998 Windows X-Wing installation; 1998 uses the main folder containing X-Wing Data, IVFiles and MUSIC. Combining 1994 menus/music and 1998 flight assets is optional. The separate 1993/B-Wing mode still needs 1994 or 1998 menus; it is not a substitute for either required supported installation. Built-in AdLib/OPL3 is available: optional MT-32/SC-55 ROMs and SoundFonts are not mandatory inputs. Keep all package resources, shaders and DLLs intact. Normal user settings, pilots, replays and temporary files belong to the current account’s SDL preference directory TotallyOpen/OpenXW; preserve that WHOLE effective profile and every original-data root. Config defaults inside resources are immutable package files, separate from user config.yaml. Core manages only the engine and the listed local config files, not shared external profiles. If SDL profile lookup fails, user/temporary output can fall back to the executable working directory. Arbitrarily named pilots, replays and cache/temp files there are unclaimed modified-runtime data: existing guards refuse destructive maintenance while retaining the creating runtime. A Core backup of declared files does not back up those unknown files. Preserve the WHOLE creating runtime and all effective profiles before reviewing recovery; do not delete files to force an update or assume re-download repairs saves. No automatic migration, portable-pilot backup, backward-save conversion or automatic recovery is offered.
